conventions.code_style: TypeScript strict; prefer pure functions; no default exports in core; zod-first types (infer from schema, never hand-duplicate).
conventions.core_purity: packages/core must not import node:fs, node:os, or network libs. All I/O flows through injected ClientAdapter / SecretProvider. Enforce with an eslint no-restricted-imports rule and a CI check.
conventions.commits: Conventional Commits. One story per branch: `story/<id>-<slug>`. Reference the story id in the commit body.
conventions.branching: Trunk-based; each story is a short-lived branch merged to main via PR that must pass CI.
conventions.testing_rule: Every story ships tests. Adapters use fixture snapshots (native config in / canonical out and back). No story is `done` until its own acceptance tests pass and the full suite is green.
conventions.error_ux: Validation and doctor errors must name the exact file, key, and fix (e.g. 'VS Code uses root key "servers", not "mcpServers"').
conventions.cross_platform: Every path-resolving function has explicit win32/darwin/linux behavior and tests. Never assume `~` expands.
conventions.security: Secret values never written to git-tracked files. `inline` strategy refuses to run unless target is gitignored, and warns loudly. Pin `@latest` at fold time when `pin` is present.

commands.verify_all: pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm -r build

loop_protocol.description: How a Ralph/Claude loop should consume this file on each iteration. One story per iteration. Never work on a story whose dependencies are not all `done`.
iteration_steps: 1. Read PROGRESS.md tail and this prd.json. Pick the highest-priority story with status `todo` (or `in_progress` you own) whose every dependency id is `done`. Respect `order` as a tiebreak.
2. If no story is eligible, stop and report which stories are blocked and by what.
3. Create/checkout branch `story/<id>-<slug>`. Set the story status to `in_progress` and append a start line to PROGRESS.md.
4. Implement ONLY that story. Touch only files consistent with `files_hint` unless the story genuinely requires more; note any deviation.
5. Write the tests named in `tests` first (or alongside). They must fail before implementation and pass after.
6. Run `verify_all`. Do not proceed until lint, typecheck, tests, and build all pass.
7. Verify every item in `acceptance_criteria` and `definition_of_done` is objectively satisfied. If a criterion is untestable as written, add a test that makes it testable.
8. Commit with a Conventional Commit referencing `<id>`. Open/refresh the PR. When CI is green, set status `done` and append a completion line (id, commit sha, summary, follow-ups) to PROGRESS.md.
9. If blocked (ambiguity, external dependency, failing infra), set status `blocked`, write the reason in PROGRESS.md, and move to the next eligible story rather than guessing.
10. Never mark `done` with a red suite, a skipped acceptance criterion, or a TODO left in shipped code.
global_definition_of_done: Tests added and the full suite green on the CI matrix (ubuntu/macos/windows where the story is platform-relevant).
Typecheck + lint clean; core purity rule not violated.
Public API changes reflected in exported types and the JSON schema if the canonical format changed.
No secret values committed; no unpinned @latest introduced where `pin` semantics apply.

stories.title: Governance & contribution scaffolding + adapter on-ramp
stories.user_story: As a would-be contributor, I want clear licensing, contribution norms, a private security-disclosure path, and a one-command way to scaffold a new client adapter, so the community can add clients as PRs without friction.
stories.context: The whole spec bets on new clients arriving as community PRs — that only happens if the on-ramp exists from commit one. Retrofitting community norms onto an active repo is disruptive; seeding them is a folder of markdown plus one generator command.
acceptance_criteria: LICENSE (MIT) on core+CLI; a NOTICE clarifying no implied MCP endorsement.
CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, and SECURITY.md with a private disclosure path (mcpfold handles secrets-adjacent config — expect reports).
GitHub issue + PR templates, including an 'adapter request' template.
docs/adapters.md tutorial 'add a new client in one PR' (ties to S8.1) exists as a stub referenced here.
`mcpfold scaffold-adapter <name>` generates a new adapter module + test + fixture skeleton that compiles and is picked up by the registry.
CODEOWNERS routes adapter dirs for review.
tests: scaffold-adapter produces a compiling, registered adapter skeleton in a tmp checkout; required governance files exist.
definition_of_done: A new contributor can scaffold an adapter and open a PR guided entirely by repo files.

stories.title: Error hierarchy + redaction-safe diagnostics (debug mode + bundle)
stories.user_story: As a user filing a bug, I want a verbose debug mode and a 'copy sanitized diagnostic bundle' command that never leaks secrets or ref paths, so I can report issues without exposing my setup.
stories.context: A single typed error hierarchy and a redaction-safe diagnostics layer must exist BEFORE any error-reporting sink (Sentry — which you already run) ships its first event, or ref paths leak into your error tracker. The redaction rule here is the same one S9.3 enforces for CLI output.
acceptance_criteria: A base McpfoldError hierarchy with codes; all thrown errors carry a code + actionable message.
`--debug` / MCPFOLD_DEBUG=1 enables verbose, still-redacted logging.
`mcpfold diagnose` (or `--bundle`) emits a sanitized diagnostic bundle: versions, detected clients, config with secret VALUES and provider ref paths redacted.
A redaction module is shared with S9.3 and, when wired, with any telemetry/Sentry sink (S8.3) so no event can contain a secret or ref path.
Test proves the bundle and debug logs contain no sentinel secret and no ref path.
tests: Bundle/debug output scrubbed of sentinel secret + ref path; each command maps failures to a coded error.
definition_of_done: Diagnostics are useful and provably leak-free before any reporting sink is added.

stories.title: Config schema versioning + `mcpfold migrate`
stories.user_story: As a user, I want my first breaking format change to be a `mcpfold migrate`, not a support fire, so the config format can evolve without stranding anyone.
stories.context: `version: 1` is in the schema but nothing defines what happens at version 2. Ship the migration-runner skeleton BEFORE v1 is widely adopted so the path is proven when you actually need it.
acceptance_criteria: A migration registry maps version N→N+1 transforms; a runner applies them in sequence.
`mcpfold migrate` detects an outdated `version`, backs up, applies migrations, and writes the upgraded config (comments preserved best-effort).
loadConfig detects a newer-than-supported version and errors with a clear 'upgrade mcpfold' message.
A no-op 1→1 identity migration + one worked example (a hypothetical 1→2) prove the pipeline end to end.
Migrations are covered by round-trip tests.
tests: Identity migration no-ops; example 1→2 transforms fixtures; newer-version config errors clearly.
definition_of_done: A format bump ships as a migration, not a breaking change.

stories.title: Deterministic, reproducible output + `--check` mode
stories.user_story: As a user, I want mcpfold's rendered files to be byte-stable given the same input so diffs are clean, snapshot tests don't thrash, and I can gate CI on 'is everything synced'.
stories.context: A determinism invariant every adapter (S2.*) and sync (S3.5) must honor: stable key ordering, consistent indentation, trailing newline. Without it, every diff is noisy from day 1.
acceptance_criteria: A shared serializer guarantees stable key order, fixed indentation, and a trailing newline for all rendered output.
Rendering the same canonical input twice is byte-identical.
`mcpfold sync --check` exits nonzero if on-disk files differ from what would be written (prettier --check style), writing nothing — CI-gateable.
The determinism invariant is documented so adapter authors follow it.
A property/fuzz-style test asserts idempotent, stable serialization across shuffled input.
tests: Double-render byte-equality; --check trips on drift and passes when clean; shuffled-key input yields identical output.
definition_of_done: Output is reproducible and CI can gate on sync freshness.

stories.title: Offline / degraded-mode contract for resolution and sync
stories.user_story: As a user, I want defined, predictable behavior when a secret provider or the network is unavailable, so a flaky Infisical or lost connection produces a clear failure, not a corrupt config.
stories.context: A secrets-resolving, cloud-syncing CLI must define what happens when Infisical is down, the network is gone, or a provider times out. Deciding the contract now shapes the resolver interface (S4.1), which is hard to change once providers depend on it.
acceptance_criteria: A documented contract: provider resolution failures fail closed (no partial/blank secret ever injected), with a specific exit code and message naming the provider + ref.
Configurable per-provider timeouts; a hung provider aborts cleanly rather than blocking indefinitely.
Operations that need no secrets/network (validate, diff of ref-only fields, doctor structural checks) still work fully offline.
Cloud commands (push/pull) degrade to a clear 'offline' error, never a silent no-op.
The resolver interface (consumed by S4.1) reflects this contract from the start.
Tests simulate provider timeout, provider error, and full offline.
tests: Timeout/error/offline each produce the defined exit code + message; offline validate/diff/doctor still succeed.
definition_of_done: Degraded behavior is defined, implemented, and tested before providers proliferate.

stories.title: Stable `--json` output + exit-code contract across all commands
stories.user_story: As someone scripting mcpfold in CI, I want a documented, versioned machine-readable output shape and consistent exit codes on every command, so my pipelines don't break when mcpfold updates.
stories.context: People will script this tool; breaking their pipelines is how OSS CLIs lose trust. Lock the contract before the audience exists. Every command (S3.*, S6.6) must conform.
acceptance_criteria: A documented exit-code convention: 0 = success/clean, 1 = actionable difference (e.g. drift), 2 = error/misuse; applied uniformly.
`--json` is supported on every command with a stable, versioned envelope ({ ok, command, data, warnings, errors }).
The JSON envelope has its own schema + snapshot tests so accidental shape changes fail CI.
Human vs JSON output paths are separated so formatting changes can't alter machine output.
A conformance test iterates all commands asserting they honor the exit-code + envelope contract.
tests: Per-command exit codes + JSON envelope conform; envelope schema snapshot guards against drift.
definition_of_done: The scripting contract is stable, documented, and enforced across every command.

stories.title: Zod canonical schema for mcp.config.jsonc
stories.user_story: As a config author, I want a strict, well-errored schema for version/servers/profiles so invalid configs fail loudly with actionable messages.
stories.context: Mirrors spec §4. Server refine: stdio needs command, http/sse needs url. SecretRef regex ^\$\{[a-z0-9_-]+:.+\}$. Profile client enum of the six clients; scope user/project/workspace; path required for project/workspace.
acceptance_criteria: Config = { version: literal(1), servers: record(Server), profiles: record(Profile) }.
Server supports transport(stdio|http|sse), command, args, url, auth(type bearer|header|none, token:SecretRef, headers), env, pin, tools({mode:allow|deny, list}), tags(default []).
Refine enforces command↔stdio and url↔http/sse with a clear message.
Profile refine requires `path` when scope is project|workspace.
All exported types are z.infer-derived (no hand-duplicated interfaces).
Parsing a valid spec-§4 example passes; each malformed variant returns a specific error.
tests: packages/core/test/schema.test.ts covering valid config + one failing case per rule (missing command, bad secret ref, missing path, bad version).
definition_of_done: Schema exported from @mcpfold/core public API with inferred types.

stories.title: JSONC loader with comment-preserving parse and located errors
stories.user_story: As a config author, I want to keep comments in mcp.config.jsonc and get errors with line/column so editing by hand is pleasant.
stories.context: Use jsonc-parser to tolerate comments/trailing commas. Map zod issues back to source positions where possible.
acceptance_criteria: loadConfig(text) parses JSONC (comments, trailing commas) then validates via the zod schema.
Parse errors report line/column and the offending token.
Validation errors include the JSON path (e.g. servers.github.auth.token) and a fix hint.
Round-trip helper preserves comments when writing back edits that don't touch commented regions (best-effort, documented).
Reading the spec §4 example (with its // comments) succeeds.
tests: JSONC with comments loads; malformed JSONC returns positioned error; invalid-but-parseable returns pathed zod error.
definition_of_done: loadConfig is the single entry point used by all consumers.

stories.title: Secret-reference grammar and parser
stories.user_story: As the engine, I want to parse ${provider:path} references so the secret resolver knows which provider and path to fetch, without resolving values yet.
stories.context: Grammar: ${scheme:path} where scheme in [env,dotenv,infisical,keychain,op] and path is provider-specific (e.g. dev/mcp/GITHUB_PAT). Pure parsing only — resolution is E4.
acceptance_criteria: parseSecretRef(str) → { scheme, path } or null for non-refs.
findSecretRefs(server) enumerates every ref in auth.token, auth.headers, and env.
Unknown scheme yields a validation-time warning surfaced to doctor, not a hard parse crash.
A string that is partly a ref (e.g. 'Bearer ${env:X}') is handled or explicitly disallowed and documented.
No network or fs access in this module.
tests: Valid refs across schemes parse; non-refs return null; enumeration finds refs in nested headers/env.
definition_of_done: Exported from core; consumed by resolver (E4) and doctor (E3).

stories.title: Profile / tag / scope resolution engine
stories.user_story: As the engine, I want to resolve a profile into the concrete set of servers (tag-filtered) with scope/path context so an adapter receives exactly what to render.

definition_of_done: Config round-trips machine→cloud→machine with refs intact and no secret values ever stored.

stories.title: Side Docker service for edge functions in Coolify
stories.user_story: As the operator, I want a standalone Dockerized Deno service running the mcpfold edge handlers so I can host functions Coolify/Supabase's managed runtime doesn't cover, sharing the same JWT/RLS contract.
stories.context: Spec stack: 'a side Docker service to run any needed edge functions'. Same code as services/edge, packaged as its own container, deployed in Coolify, verifying Supabase JWTs and honoring RLS via the service/anon keys appropriately.
acceptance_criteria: A Dockerfile builds a Deno service exposing the same auth/push/pull handlers over HTTP.
It verifies Supabase-issued JWTs and enforces the same access rules (no privilege bypass).
Health check endpoint + graceful shutdown.
Coolify deployment documented with env/secret wiring (no secrets in the image).
An integration test hits the container in CI (docker-compose) for a push/pull cycle.
tests: Container starts, health check passes, authenticated push/pull works, unauthenticated is rejected.
definition_of_done: Side service reaches feature parity with the edge functions and passes CI integration.

stories.title: CLI login / push / pull commands
stories.user_story: As a user, I want `mcpfold login`, `push`, and `pull` so my canonical config syncs across machines from the CLI.
stories.context: Spec §8/§9. login runs device-code OAuth (S6.3) and stores the token in keychain; push/pull call the edge/side service; pull can diff before applying.
acceptance_criteria: `mcpfold login` completes device-code flow and stores the session in the OS keychain.
`mcpfold push` uploads the local canonical config (refs only) as a new version, tagged with this machine.
`mcpfold pull` fetches latest, shows a diff vs local (reusing S1.6), and applies on confirmation (or --yes).
All commands fail clearly when not logged in or when the endpoint is unreachable.
Never uploads resolved secret values (client-side guard mirrors the server guard).
tests: Against a mocked endpoint: login stores token; push sends refs-only; pull diffs + applies; logged-out errors.
definition_of_done: Two-machine sync works end to end against the local stack.

stories.title: Web app scaffold on Cloudflare Pages + Supabase auth
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to log into mcpfold.com and see my account so the web console has a foundation.
stories.context: Spec §9. React + TS + Vite on Cloudflare Pages; Supabase auth (session from GoTrue). Shared canonical types imported from @mcpfold/core.
acceptance_criteria: apps/web builds with Vite and deploys to Cloudflare Pages (documented + a preview deploy in CI).
Supabase auth login/logout works against the self-hosted instance.
Authenticated routes gated; unauthenticated redirected to login.
Reuses @mcpfold/core types (no duplicated config types in the frontend).
Basic responsive shell + theme.
tests: Playwright: login flow and gated route redirect.
definition_of_done: A user can log in on a Pages preview deploy.

stories.title: Visual canonical-config editor
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to edit my mcp.config.jsonc visually — add/edit servers, auth refs, tags — with validation, and push it.
stories.context: Spec §9. Form + JSON views backed by the shared zod schema; edits validate client-side; save pushes a new version. Secret fields accept refs only.
acceptance_criteria: CRUD servers with transport-aware fields (stdio vs http/sse) validated by the shared schema.
Auth/token fields accept ${provider:path} refs only; raw values blocked with guidance.
Live validation surfaces the same errors as the CLI (shared schema).
Save creates a new config version via push (S6.4) and shows version history.
Optimistic UI with error rollback.
tests: Playwright: add a server, invalid token blocked, save creates a version.
definition_of_done: Edits persist as new versions and validate identically to the CLI.

stories.title: Profile management UI
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to create and edit profiles (client + scope + tag include set) visually so I control what folds where.
stories.context: Spec §4/§9. Editor for profiles with client/scope/path/include; previews which servers a profile resolves to (reusing resolve logic).
acceptance_criteria: Create/edit/delete profiles with client, scope, path, include tags.
Live preview lists the servers a profile would resolve to (server-level curation visualization).
Validation mirrors the schema (path required for project/workspace).
Changes persist via push.
tests: Playwright: create a profile, preview resolves the expected servers.
definition_of_done: Profiles editable and their fold preview is correct.

stories.title: Curated server directory
stories.user_story: As a user, I want a browsable directory of known MCP servers so I can add them to my config with one click.
stories.context: Spec §9 monetizable surface (public directory now; private registry later). Directory entries prefill the add flow with transport, url/package, and suggested tools.
acceptance_criteria: Browse/search a seeded directory of MCP servers.
'Add to config' prefills the editor with a valid server entry (token as a ref placeholder).
Directory data is seeded and versioned; adding new entries is a documented process.
Respects the 'no implied endorsement' copy rule.
tests: Playwright: search + add-to-config prefills a valid entry.

stories.title: Per-machine sync status dashboard
stories.user_story: As a user with multiple machines, I want to see each machine's last sync, version, and drift so I know everything is consistent.
stories.context: Spec §9. Reads machines + configs history to show which version each machine last pushed/pulled.
acceptance_criteria: Lists registered machines with last-seen, last pushed/pulled version.
Flags machines behind the latest version.
Shows recent version history with author + timestamp.
Data scoped by RLS to the current user/team.
tests: Playwright: dashboard shows machines and highlights an out-of-date one.
definition_of_done: Sync status reflects real push/pull activity.

stories.title: Team console + change-audit trail
stories.user_story: As a team lead, I want shared team configs and an audit trail of who changed what, when, so governance is clear — the paid surface.
stories.context: Spec §9 monetization. Team-shared configs with member management and the append-only audit view ('who added the Stripe server, when').
acceptance_criteria: Create a team, invite/manage members (roles), share a team config.
Audit trail lists every config change with author, timestamp, and a diff.
RLS enforces team-scoped access; non-members cannot read team configs.
Billing gate stub marks this as a paid feature (integration deferred).
Member removal revokes access immediately.
tests: Playwright + RLS: member sees team config, non-member denied, audit shows a change diff.

stories.title: Docs site, README, and hosted JSON schema
stories.user_story: As a prospective user, I want clear docs — the format spec, quickstart, adapter authoring guide — and a hosted $schema URL so onboarding is frictionless.
stories.context: Spec §2/§10. Publish the neutral mcp.config.jsonc format spec, the CLI quickstart (init→import→sync loop), and host the generated JSON schema.
acceptance_criteria: docs/ covers: format spec, quickstart, secrets, adapter authoring, benchmark.
README leads with the context-window benchmark, not sync.
The generated JSON schema is hosted at a stable URL and referenced by init's scaffold.
An 'add a new client adapter in one PR' guide exists.
Docs build in CI.
tests: Docs build + link-check pass in CI; schema URL resolves.
definition_of_done: A newcomer can go init→import→sync from docs alone.

stories.title: Cross-platform end-to-end test suite
stories.user_story: As a maintainer, I want e2e tests exercising the real init→import→sync→diff loop in temp dirs on all three OSes so path bugs never ship.
stories.context: Spec §10 format-drift risk. Full CLI lifecycle against fixture client files in isolated tmp HOME dirs, on the CI matrix.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: init → add fixture client files → import → sync → diff (clean) → mutate on-disk → diff (drift) in a tmp HOME.
Runs on ubuntu/macos/windows with correct per-OS paths.
Backups verified created before overwrite.
Secret strategies verified to leave no secret values on disk.
Suite is stable (no flakes) and reasonably fast.
tests: The lifecycle test itself, green on all three OSes.
definition_of_done: Full loop green on the matrix.

stories.title: Security review, telemetry opt-in, and hardening
stories.user_story: As a security-conscious user, I want assurance that mcpfold never leaks secrets, pins supply-chain risk, and only collects telemetry I opt into.
stories.context: Spec §6/§10. Audit secret handling end to end, enforce pin-at-fold, and make any telemetry strictly opt-in with a documented payload.
acceptance_criteria: A documented audit confirms no code path writes a resolved secret to a git-tracked file or logs it.
`pin` rewrites @latest to the pinned version at fold time; a test proves an unpinned @latest is flagged by doctor.
Telemetry (if any) is opt-in only, with a documented, minimal, non-secret payload and an easy opt-out.
Dependency + secret-scanning checks run in CI (e.g. gitleaks + npm audit).
A threat-model note covers the shim launcher and proxy surfaces.
tests: Secret-leak grep test across rendered outputs; doctor flags unpinned; gitleaks clean.
definition_of_done: Security posture documented and enforced in CI.

stories.title: OSS launch: npm publish + awesome-mcp + Show HN readiness
stories.user_story: As the maintainer, I want the v0.x packages published and launch surfaces prepped so I can post and gather traction.
stories.context: Spec §10 launch. Publish MIT core+CLI, submit to awesome-mcp lists, prep Show HN/dev.to/r/mcp with the benchmark headline, and open the WG config-portability thread with running code.
acceptance_criteria: `npx mcpfold` installs and runs the init→import→sync loop from the published package.
Semver + changelog generated via changesets; release notes reference the benchmark.
awesome-mcp PR drafted; Show HN / dev.to draft prepared with the context-window numbers.
A WG discussion thread draft references the shipping reference implementation and neutral format.
Post-install smoke test in CI verifies the published tarball works.
tests: CI installs the packed tarball and runs a smoke lifecycle.
definition_of_done: A real `npx mcpfold` run works from npm; launch collateral ready.

stories.title: End-to-end deployment runbook + cloud env bootstrap
stories.user_story: As the operator standing up mcpfold, I want one runbook that takes me from zero to a fully running stack (both Cloudflare Pages front ends, self-hosted Supabase, the side edge container, and npm publishing) plus a script that generates every secret, so I can go live without piecing it together from per-subsystem docs.
stories.context: The per-subsystem docs exist (self-hosting, coolify-edge-service, site-hosting, security-at-rest) but nothing ties them into a single go-live sequence with the full environment matrix and the non-obvious cross-cutting facts: JWT_SECRET is the shared trust anchor across Supabase + edge + the web anon key, and api.mcpfold.com must path-split between the Kong gateway (/auth/v1, /rest/v1, /realtime/v1) and the edge service (/auth-device, /push, /pull, /teams, ...). docs/deployment.md (the runbook + env matrix + go-live checklist) and scripts/gen-cloud-env.sh (generates the random secrets and mints the Supabase ANON_KEY/SERVICE_ROLE_KEY as HS256 JWTs signed with the generated JWT_SECRET, then prints ready-to-paste env blocks) already exist from this work; this story wires their verification and keeps them accurate.
acceptance_criteria: docs/deployment.md documents the architecture, DNS, the api.mcpfold.com path-split, a per-surface environment-variable matrix, the ordered go-live steps, per-surface smoke checks, and a pre-launch checklist, cross-linking the deeper docs (no forked duplication).

scripts/gen-cloud-env.sh generates POSTGRES_PASSWORD/JWT_SECRET/REALTIME keys and mints valid HS256 ANON_KEY + SERVICE_ROLE_KEY signed with the generated JWT_SECRET, printing paste-ready blocks for Supabase, the edge service, and the web Pages project.
The env-var list in the runbook stays in sync with the real sources (supabase/.env.example, apps/web/.env.example, services/edge, the workflows) - a check flags drift between them.
A docs link-check covers deployment.md (every relative link resolves), consistent with the S8.1 docs gate.
The generated ANON_KEY verifies as a valid Supabase JWT (signature + role/iss/exp) in a test, and shellcheck is clean on the script.
tests: gen-cloud-env.sh output parses and the minted ANON_KEY signature verifies against JWT_SECRET; env-matrix drift check trips on a planted mismatch; deployment.md link-check passes.
definition_of_done: An operator can go from a fresh domain + VPS to a verified, fully running stack using only docs/deployment.md and scripts/gen-cloud-env.sh.

stories.title: Ref-only invariant: suite-wide secret-leak assertion harness
stories.user_story: As a security-conscious maintainer, I want an automated harness that proves no resolved secret value ever lands in a rendered client file, a backup, a temp file, a log line, or a pushed payload, so the core promise is continuously enforced, not just claimed.
stories.context: The single most important control. Seed every test path with a known sentinel secret value (e.g. SENTINEL_TOKEN_deadbeef), exercise sync/run/diff/doctor/push across all adapters and strategies, then assert the sentinel appears in ZERO artifacts except where an explicitly gitignored `inline` target legitimately holds it. Resolution must be memory-only — no cache-to-disk of values, ever.
acceptance_criteria: A shared harness injects a sentinel value via a fake provider and scans all rendered files, backups, temp dirs, stdout/stderr, and push payloads for it.
Passes for env/dotenv/infisical/keychain/op providers and shim + native-input strategies (sentinel must NOT appear).
For `inline`, the sentinel may appear only in the target file AND only when that file is gitignored; the harness asserts both.
A client-side guard rejects a push payload containing any non-ref value in a secret position (mirrors the server guard in S6.4); test proves rejection.
Asserts no resolved value is written to any on-disk cache/temp (resolution is memory-only).
Runs on the CI matrix; a deliberately introduced leak fails the build.
tests: Sentinel-scan across all strategies/providers; inline gated on gitignore; push guard rejects raw value; injected leak fails.
definition_of_done: The ref-only invariant is machine-verified on every relevant path in CI.

stories.title: Config-as-code: trust-on-first-use + version integrity signing
stories.user_story: As a user syncing config across machines, I want any new or changed executable command to require my confirmation and every pushed version to be integrity-verified, so a tampered or malicious synced config cannot silently execute code on my machines.
stories.context: `mcpfold run` execs command/args from the config, and `pull` writes that config from the cloud — a code-execution channel. Combine TOFU (like SSH host keys) with signed versions. Same threat class as the unpinned-stdio-RCE lesson, but via the sync path.
acceptance_criteria: sync/pull detect any new or changed `command`, `args`, or `pin` and require explicit confirmation before those entries become runnable; a local trust store records approved entries.
`--yes` (CI) can pre-approve, and is documented as reducing this protection.
Each pushed config version is signed (HMAC with a per-user key or Ed25519); pull verifies the signature and refuses/warns on mismatch.
A tampered version row (unsigned or bad signature) is rejected by the client.
`pin` may carry an optional integrity hash for the stdio package; a mismatch is flagged.
Trust prompts and signature failures are covered by tests using a mocked endpoint.
tests: Changed command triggers prompt; approved entry runs without re-prompt; bad signature rejected; hash mismatch flagged.
definition_of_done: Cloud-synced config cannot execute new commands without explicit trust, and version integrity is verified.

stories.title: Output redaction + backup hardening for the inline path
stories.user_story: As a user, I want all CLI output and any backup files to never expose a secret, so diagnostics and the inline fallback can't leak what the ref-only design otherwise protects.
stories.context: diff/doctor print file contents and sync backs up prior files (.mcpfold.bak) — both can capture or echo an inlined secret. Redact output and harden backups.
acceptance_criteria: All diff/doctor/log output masks values that resolve through a provider and any high-entropy token-shaped string.
Backups of a file that could contain an inlined secret are created gitignored and chmod 600 (0600) on POSIX, ACL-restricted on Windows — or the backup is refused with a clear message.
`inline` strategy refuses to write unless the target is gitignored AND emits a loud warning (reaffirms S4.6) — regression-tested here.
A redaction unit test proves masked output for each output command.
No secret-shaped string survives in any command's stdout/stderr in the leak harness (ties to S9.1).
tests: diff/doctor mask a token; backup perms/gitignore enforced or refused; inline refusal path.
definition_of_done: No CLI output or backup can expose a secret value.

stories.title: Self-hosted at-rest hardening: volume encryption, encrypted backups, TLS/HSTS
stories.user_story: As the operator of self-hosted Supabase on Contabo, I want documented + verified volume encryption, encrypted DB backups, and enforced TLS so at-rest and in-transit protection match a managed provider's baseline.
stories.context: Self-hosting means YOU own disk encryption — managed Supabase gives it free. Because configs are refs-only, a DB dump leaks topology + ref paths (per the chosen server-side-at-rest model), never secret values; document that explicitly as a design property.
acceptance_criteria: A runbook enables volume/disk encryption (LUKS or equivalent) for the Postgres data volume in the Coolify deployment.
Automated Postgres backups are encrypted at rest and their restore is tested.
TLS is enforced end to end (Pages→edge→DB where applicable); HSTS set on web/API responses.
A documented threat statement: 'DB compromise exposes config metadata (server names, URLs, ref paths), never secret values.'
A verification step (script or checklist) confirms encryption + TLS are actually on, not just configured.
tests: Backup encrypt+restore round-trip test; TLS/HSTS header assertion against the running stack in CI.
definition_of_done: At-rest + in-transit protections verified on the self-hosted stack.

stories.title: Session & device-code hardening + machine revocation
stories.user_story: As a user, I want short-lived rotated sessions, a phishing-resistant device-code flow, and the ability to revoke any machine, so a stolen token or intercepted code has minimal blast radius.
stories.context: Device-code flows are phishable and long-lived tokens are dangerous. Harden the flow from S6.3 and expose revocation in the sync dashboard (S7.5).
acceptance_criteria: Access tokens are short-lived with refresh rotation; refresh reuse is detected and revokes the chain.
Device-code: high-entropy user code, short expiry, poll-endpoint rate limiting, and binding to the requesting machine id.
Per-machine token revocation from the sync dashboard immediately invalidates that machine's sessions.
All sync/auth endpoints enforce JWT + RLS and rate-limit abusive callers.
Tests cover expiry, refresh rotation/reuse-detection, rate-limit, and revocation.
tests: Expired/rotated/reused tokens handled; rate limit trips; revoked machine denied.
definition_of_done: Session + device-code surfaces hardened and revocation works end to end.

stories.title: Web app security headers + dependency/secret scanning gate
stories.user_story: As a user of mcpfold.com, I want standard web hardening (CSP, HSTS, anti-CSRF) and a CI gate that blocks leaked secrets and known-vulnerable dependencies, so the cloud surface meets a baseline OWASP posture.
stories.context: Consolidates web + supply-chain hygiene into an enforced gate (extends the lighter S8.3). Team-invite and share tokens must be high-entropy; access revocation on member removal is already required in S7.6.
acceptance_criteria: apps/web sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and frame protections; anti-CSRF on state-changing requests.
Team-invite / share tokens are high-entropy and single-use/expiring.
CI runs gitleaks + dependency audit (npm audit / OSV) and fails on high-severity findings or any detected secret.
A threat-model doc covers the shim launcher, proxy, and sync channel surfaces.
Header presence asserted by an automated test against the deployed preview.
tests: Header assertions on the running app; CI security gate trips on a planted secret / vulnerable dep.
definition_of_done: Web hardening in place and the security gate enforced in CI.

stories.title: `mcpfold status` - unified health + sync front door
stories.user_story: As a user, I want one command that answers 'is my setup OK?' - detected clients, drift per client, login/sync state, and outstanding warnings - so mcpfold has a daily front door instead of a pile of subcommands.
stories.context: The toolbox has no cohesion command; after the one-time migration there is no reason to reopen it. status aggregates existing engines (diff for drift, doctor for footguns, cloud session for login/last-sync) into a single scannable summary; strictly read-only. Honors the --json envelope and exit-code contract (S0.10).
acceptance_criteria: Lists each detected client with: managed/unmanaged, in-sync vs drifted (server + field counts), and needsRestart hint.
Summarizes canonical-config health (doctor error/warn counts) and flags unpinned/insecure entries without a full doctor dump.
Shows cloud state when applicable: logged-in identity, last push/pull version, behind/ahead status.
Read-only: never writes files or backups; safe to run anytime.
--json emits the stable envelope; exit 0 when clean/in-sync, 1 when actionable drift or warnings exist, 2 on error.
tests: Clean tmp HOME -> all in-sync, exit 0; mutate one client file -> drift shown, exit 1; logged-out hides cloud section; --json shape stable.
definition_of_done: status is the single command that summarizes local + cloud health at a glance.

stories.title: `mcpfold sync --watch` - background auto-fold on config change
stories.user_story: As a user, I want mcpfold to re-fold my clients automatically when mcp.config.jsonc changes, so keeping every client in sync is a background habit rather than a command I forget to run.
stories.context: Converts the one-time migration tool into a daily driver. A debounced file watcher on the canonical config re-runs sync, reusing the atomic-write + backup path and respecting --profile, --dry-run, and the determinism invariant (S0.8).
acceptance_criteria: --watch observes mcp.config.jsonc and re-syncs affected profiles on change, debounced to coalesce rapid edits.
Each auto-sync backs up and writes atomically exactly as a manual sync; no half-written files on rapid saves.
Clean shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM; a summary line per fold; --dry-run watches and prints diffs without writing.
Errors during a watched fold (e.g. invalid config mid-edit) are reported and never crash the watcher or leave partial output.
Cross-platform watching works on win32/darwin/linux (tested via an injectable fs-event abstraction).
tests: Editing the config triggers one debounced re-sync; invalid intermediate config is reported without crashing; SIGINT stops cleanly.
definition_of_done: Auto-sync keeps every client current without manual re-runs.

stories.title: Guided first-run onboarding (`mcpfold init --guided`)
stories.user_story: As a brand-new user, I want a guided flow that walks me from zero to synced - detect clients, import what I have, fix footguns, sync, and show my context savings - so the first five minutes prove the value.
stories.context: init today scaffolds a file; nothing walks a newcomer through the golden path. A guided flow chains init -> import -> doctor (with offered fixes) -> sync -> a before/after context-window number (S5.4), each step skippable and non-interactive-flag friendly.
acceptance_criteria: Detects installed clients, offers to import existing configs, and previews the merge before writing.
Runs doctor inline and offers to apply safe fixes (rewrite plaintext tokens to refs, pin @latest) with confirmation.
Ends by syncing and printing the context-window before/after for the resolved set, linking to the benchmark.
Every prompt has a non-interactive flag/default so the flow is scriptable and CI-safe; --dry-run shows the whole plan.
Never clobbers an existing canonical config without confirmation; safe to abort at any step with no partial writes.
tests: Scripted guided run in a tmp HOME with fixture clients: imports, fixes a footgun, syncs, prints savings; abort leaves no partial writes.
definition_of_done: A newcomer reaches a synced, secure, measurably-lighter setup in one guided flow.

stories.title: `mcpfold test <server>` - live MCP handshake + health check
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to actually connect to a configured server and confirm it initializes and lists tools, so 'doctor says valid' becomes 'this server really works'.
stories.context: doctor validates structure; nothing verifies a server actually responds. Reusing the proxy transports (S5.1), test resolves a server, performs the MCP initialize handshake + tools/list, and reports reachability, tool count, and any auth failure - resolving secrets in-memory only, never printing values.
acceptance_criteria: test <server> resolves the server (secrets in-memory), opens the correct transport (stdio/http/sse), and performs the MCP initialize + tools/list handshake.
Reports reachable/unreachable, negotiated protocol, and tool count; with no arg, tests all servers in the active profile.
Auth/connection failures produce a clear, actionable message that never echoes the resolved token.
Bounded per-server timeout (reuses the offline/degraded contract S0.9); a hung server aborts cleanly.
--json emits a per-server result array; exit nonzero if any tested server fails.
tests: Against an in-memory/mock MCP server: healthy server reports tool count; unreachable + auth-failure paths reported without leaking the token; timeout aborts.
definition_of_done: Users can confirm a server truly works, not just that its config parses.

stories.title: `mcpfold restore` - first-class rollback from backups
stories.user_story: As a user, I want to roll back a client file to a mcpfold backup with one command, so I can undo a bad sync without hunting for timestamped .bak files by hand.
stories.context: sync writes timestamped <path>.mcpfold.bak.<ts> backups but there is no restore verb. restore lists available backups per client and restores a chosen one atomically, honoring the backup-hardening rules (permissions, gitignore) from S9.3.
acceptance_criteria: Lists available backups per client with timestamps; --list shows them without restoring.
Restores the selected (or latest) backup atomically, backing up the current file first so restore is itself reversible.
Respects the S9.3 backup permission/redaction rules; refuses to expose or mishandle a possibly-inlined secret.
Handles missing/corrupt backups with a clear error; --dry-run shows what would be restored.
--json output and exit codes follow the contract.
tests: Sync creates a backup -> mutate -> restore returns the prior contents; latest-vs-chosen selection; missing backup errors; dry-run writes nothing.
definition_of_done: Any sync is one command away from being undone.

stories.title: Multi-channel install: Homebrew, curl|sh, Scoop/winget, standalone binaries
stories.user_story: As a user who won't npx a random package, I want to install mcpfold via Homebrew, a curl|sh script, Scoop/winget, or a standalone binary, so distribution isn't limited to the npm audience.
stories.context: S8.4 ships npm only. Broaden reach: build standalone binaries (per-OS/arch) in the release pipeline, publish a Homebrew tap and a Scoop/winget manifest, and host a checksummed curl|sh installer - all driven off the same tagged release so versions never diverge.
acceptance_criteria: Release CI builds standalone binaries for macOS (arm64/x64), Linux (x64/arm64), and Windows (x64), with checksums.
A Homebrew tap formula and a Scoop/winget manifest install the current release and update automatically on publish.
A hosted install.sh (curl|sh) verifies a checksum before installing and supports a pinned version.
Every channel resolves to the same version as the npm publish for a given tag (a CI check asserts parity).
Install docs cover all channels with copy-paste commands.
tests: CI installs each artifact on its OS and runs `mcpfold --version`; checksum verification fails closed on a tampered binary; version-parity check across channels.
definition_of_done: A user can install mcpfold through their preferred channel and get the same version.

stories.title: Shell completions (bash/zsh/fish/pwsh)
stories.user_story: As a CLI user, I want tab completion for commands, flags, profile names, and server names, so mcpfold feels like a first-class tool.
stories.context: Standard CLI table stakes. Generate completions from the command tree, expose `mcpfold completions <shell>`, and complete dynamic values (profiles, server names) from the local canonical config where cheap.
acceptance_criteria: `mcpfold completions <bash|zsh|fish|pwsh>` prints a valid completion script for that shell.
Completes subcommands and global/command flags.
Completes dynamic --profile and server-name arguments from the local config when present.
Per-shell install instructions documented.
Completion generation is covered by a snapshot test per shell.
tests: Snapshot the generated script per shell; dynamic profile/server completion resolves from a fixture config.
definition_of_done: Tab completion works in all four supported shells.

stories.title: Update notifier
stories.user_story: As a user, I want a quiet heads-up when a newer mcpfold is available, so I stay current without polling npm.
stories.context: A non-blocking, cached, opt-out-able check comparing the running version to the latest published version, printing a one-line notice with the upgrade command for the detected install channel. Must never block a command, leak anything, or run in CI/non-TTY by default.
acceptance_criteria: Checks the latest version at most once per interval, cached to disk; never blocks or delays the actual command.
Prints a single, dismissable notice naming the new version and the correct upgrade command for how mcpfold was installed.
Disabled automatically in non-TTY/CI and via an env opt-out (aligned with the S8.3 telemetry/DO_NOT_TRACK conventions).
Failure to reach the registry is silent (never an error).
No config, path, or identifying data is sent; only a version is fetched.
tests: Newer version -> notice with channel-correct command; up-to-date -> silent; offline -> silent; CI/non-TTY -> disabled; opt-out honored.
definition_of_done: Users learn about updates without friction or privacy cost.

stories.title: Scripted terminal demo (VHS/asciinema) for README + site
stories.user_story: As a prospective user skimming the README or landing page, I want a short looping demo of import -> sync -> context savings, so I grasp the value in fifteen seconds.
stories.context: S8.4's launch collateral is text only; adoption on HN/Reddit hinges on a visual. A committed, regenerable VHS tape (or asciinema cast) records the golden path against fixtures and produces a GIF/SVG embedded in README and the marketing site.
acceptance_criteria: A committed demo script (VHS .tape or asciinema cast) drives init/import -> sync -> diff(clean) -> benchmark against deterministic fixtures.
A documented command regenerates the recording so it never drifts from real CLI output.
The rendered asset (GIF/SVG) is embedded in README and available to the marketing site.
The demo leads with the context-window number and respects the no-implied-endorsement rule.
Recording runs in CI (or a documented local step) to catch a broken demo before release.
tests: The demo script runs to completion against fixtures and produces a non-empty asset; regeneration is deterministic.
definition_of_done: A regenerable 15-second demo exists for launch surfaces.

stories.title: Adoption learning loop: opt-in anonymous adapter/provider signal
stories.user_story: As the maintainer, I want a privacy-preserving, opt-in signal of which clients and providers people actually use, so I prioritize adapter work with data instead of guessing.
stories.context: S8.3 built opt-in telemetry infra with no sink, so launch is blind. Extend it with a strictly opt-in, aggregate-only event (which adapters were detected/synced, which provider schemes used) - no config, paths, URLs, server names, or secrets - plus a private aggregation view to guide the S14.1 coverage roadmap.
acceptance_criteria: Off by default; opt-in only, honoring the same DO_NOT_TRACK/opt-out precedence as S8.3.

Payload is a fixed allow-list of non-identifying fields (adapter ids present, provider schemes used, coarse counts) and reuses the S0.6 redactor as a final guard; a test proves no secret/path/name can appear.
A documented, private aggregation endpoint/view rolls events into 'which clients/providers matter' without per-user tracking.
The exact collected fields are documented publicly and easy to audit.
Injectable sink so the loop is testable with no network.
tests: Opt-out -> nothing sent; opt-in payload contains only allow-listed aggregate fields; redactor blocks a planted secret/path/name.
definition_of_done: Adapter prioritization is driven by opt-in aggregate data, not guesswork.

stories.title: Repo config-as-code convention + team drift-gate workflow
stories.user_story: As a team, I want to commit one mcp.config.jsonc to our repo and have every developer fold it locally with a CI check that fails on drift, so we standardize MCP setups with no backend.
stories.context: The PRD jumps from single-user CLI straight to the hosted cloud, skipping the obvious middle: a repo-committed canonical config as the team source of truth. Combine the existing --check drift gate (S0.8), diff (S3.6), and trust model (S9.2) into a documented team workflow - the collaboration wedge that needs no cloud and funnels toward it.
acceptance_criteria: A documented convention for a repo-committed mcp.config.jsonc (project scope) that developers fold locally.
`mcpfold sync --check` / `diff --check` is the CI gate: nonzero when a checkout's clients would drift from the committed config.
The config-as-code trust prompt (S9.2) covers a teammate adding/changing an executable command; --yes documented for CI.
A worked example repo/dir shows the whole loop (commit config -> teammate folds -> CI gate).
Docs explain how this graduates to the hosted cloud (teams, audit) without changing the config format.
tests: Example repo: matching checkout passes the gate; a drifted client fails it; a new command triggers the trust prompt.
definition_of_done: A team can standardize MCP setups from a repo with a CI drift gate and no backend.

stories.title: `mcpfold-action` packaged GitHub Action
stories.user_story: As a team, I want a ready-made GitHub Action that runs the mcpfold drift/doctor gate on pull requests, so enforcing our MCP config standard is one workflow snippet.
stories.context: Packages the S12.1 workflow as a reusable Action (composite or Docker) that installs mcpfold, runs diff/doctor --check + --json, and annotates the PR with findings. Published and versioned alongside the CLI.
acceptance_criteria: A published action.yml runs mcpfold checks with inputs for profile, working directory, and check level.
Emits PR annotations/summary from the --json output and sets the job status to the CLI exit code.
Pinned to a released mcpfold version, with a documented tag/version policy.
A self-test workflow in this repo exercises the Action on a fixture (clean pass + drift fail).
README/usage snippet copy-pasteable into any repo.
tests: Self-test workflow: clean fixture passes, drifted fixture fails with annotations.
definition_of_done: Any repo can enforce mcpfold config standards via one Action.

stories.title: Marketing site scaffold, design system, and deploy pipeline

A shared design system (tokens, typography, components) + responsive layout shell with light/dark theme.
SEO baseline on every route: title/description, Open Graph/Twitter cards, canonical URLs, robots.txt, and a generated sitemap.
Privacy-friendly analytics (no PII, no cookie wall) wired in and documented.
Routing/hosting decided so the site (root), docs (/docs), and app coexist without conflicting paths; documented.
A Lighthouse/perf budget (performance + accessibility thresholds) is checked in CI.
tests: Playwright: homepage renders, theme toggles, OG tags present; CI perf/a11y budget passes on the preview.
definition_of_done: A themed, SEO-ready site shell deploys to Pages and hosts the rest of E13.

stories.title: Hero + interactive context-window benchmark ('the tax')

acceptance_criteria: Hero leads with the context-window benchmark and a primary install CTA + secondary cloud CTA.
An interactive calculator shows before/after tool count and token/context savings using the S5.4 methodology (client-side, no secrets).
The S11.4 demo recording is embedded above the fold or one scroll down.
Numbers are sourced from the committed benchmark so the site and docs never disagree; copy respects no-implied-endorsement.
Fully responsive and accessible (keyboard + screen-reader for the calculator).

stories.title: Install + get-started page (all channels)

acceptance_criteria: Shows install commands for every channel with one-click copy and auto-highlights the visitor's likely OS.
Links straight into the quickstart (init/import/sync) and the guided onboarding.
Version shown reflects the latest release (sourced, not hardcoded).
Verified/checksum guidance surfaced for the curl|sh and binary paths.
Responsive + accessible.

definition_of_done: Every install channel is one copy-paste away with a clear next step.

stories.title: Docs integrated under unified site nav + search

acceptance_criteria: Docs render under /docs inside the marketing shell (shared nav/theme), reusing the S8.1 content pipeline (no forked copies).
Client-side search over docs content.
The existing docs link-check + build gate still runs and blocks on breakage.
The hosted JSON schema URL (/schema/v1.json) remains stable and served.
Deep links and heading anchors continue to resolve.

stories.title: Public SEO server directory with add-to-config deep links

Each entry offers 'add to config' that deep-links to the add flow (CLI command snippet and/or app editor prefill), token as a ref placeholder.
Directory data is shared/seeded with S7.4 (single source), and adding entries is documented.
Per-entry OG cards and sitemap inclusion for discoverability.
Respects no-implied-endorsement copy.

definition_of_done: The public directory is a browsable, indexable discovery + add surface.

stories.title: Pricing page + cloud signup funnel
stories.user_story: As a team lead evaluating mcpfold, I want a clear pricing page contrasting free OSS with the paid team cloud, and a signup CTA, so I can decide and convert.

FAQ covering self-hosting, licensing (MIT core, commercial cloud), and refs-only data handling.
Pricing figures/tiers come from the S14.3 model (single source), not ad-hoc copy.
Responsive + accessible.

stories.title: Blog + changelog / release notes
stories.user_story: As a follower of the project, I want a blog and a changelog on the site, so I can track releases, launches, and deep-dives like the benchmark writeup.

A changelog page rendering release notes derived from the changesets/CHANGELOG source (not hand-maintained twice).
Posts and changelog are in the sitemap and searchable.
Authoring a new post is a documented one-file process.
Responsive + accessible.
tests: Playwright: blog index + a post render with OG tags and RSS; changelog reflects the CHANGELOG source.
definition_of_done: The site has a living blog + changelog wired to real release data.

stories.title: Adapter coverage roadmap + prioritized expansion
stories.user_story: As the maintainer, I want a living, data-informed adapter coverage roadmap and a batch of the next highest-demand clients shipped, so breadth (the moat) keeps pace with the ecosystem.
stories.context: Six adapters is a start; breadth is the moat and it decays as new clients appear. Maintain a public coverage matrix and ship the next tranche of high-demand clients (candidates: Cline, Continue, Warp, Goose, Gemini CLI, JetBrains AI, Cody), prioritized by the S11.5 usage signal + community requests, each via the existing scaffold-adapter on-ramp.
acceptance_criteria: A published coverage matrix (supported clients, scope support, secret strategy, restart semantics) kept current.
At least the top-requested additional clients are implemented via scaffold-adapter, each with fixtures + round-trip in the S2.8 matrix.
Prioritization references the S11.5 opt-in signal and open adapter requests, documented.
Each new adapter passes the shared determinism + round-trip invariants.
The 'add a client in one PR' on-ramp is validated by at least one of these landing as a community-style PR.
tests: New adapters pass the cross-adapter matrix (render snapshot + round-trip); coverage matrix generated/checked.
definition_of_done: Adapter breadth is tracked and actively extended to the clients people use.

stories.title: Live-client compatibility test harness
stories.user_story: As a maintainer, I want to detect when a client changes its on-disk config format upstream, so mcpfold breaks loudly in CI instead of silently for users.
stories.context: Adapters are pinned to committed fixtures; if a client updates its config schema, mcpfold can silently produce a file the client no longer accepts. A scheduled harness checks each adapter's assumptions against the latest known client format/schema (or a captured sample) and flags divergence.
acceptance_criteria: A scheduled CI job checks each adapter's rendered shape against the current upstream client format/schema (pulled or captured), per client.
Divergence opens/updates a tracking issue naming the client, the changed key/shape, and the affected adapter.
Where a client publishes a schema, validate rendered output against it; otherwise compare against a versioned captured sample with a documented refresh process.
The job is resilient to network/source unavailability (skips with a warning, never a false failure).
A deliberately outdated fixture is detected by the harness (self-test).
tests: Self-test: a planted format change is flagged; source-unavailable path skips cleanly.
definition_of_done: Upstream client format drift surfaces in CI before it reaches users.

stories.title: Business layer: pricing model, billing path, sponsorship, roadmap

Define free-OSS vs paid tiers and limits, choose a billing path (e.g. Stripe) to integrate later, set up sponsorship (GitHub Sponsors/OpenCollective) for the MIT project, and publish a roadmap + governance doc. Deliverable is decisions + scaffolding, not full billing implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A documented pricing/packaging model: what is free forever vs paid, tiers, and limits - the single source S13.6 renders.
A billing integration decision + stubbed path (provider chosen, entitlement-check interface defined) so S7.6's billing gate can be wired later.
Sponsorship set up (GitHub Sponsors and/or OpenCollective) and linked from README + site.
A public roadmap + light governance/maintainership doc (how decisions and releases are made).
Licensing boundaries restated: MIT core/CLI, commercial cloud.

definition_of_done: The business model, billing path, funding, and roadmap are defined and published.

stories.title: True content prerender (SSG) + JSON-LD structured data
stories.user_story: As a crawler or AI answer engine that does not run JavaScript, I want every marketing route to serve its real content and structured data in the initial HTML, so mcpfold is indexable and citable instead of an empty SPA shell.
stories.context: The single highest-leverage SEO/GEO fix. Today gen-seo.mjs only string-replaces <title>/meta on the SPA shell - the <body> stays an empty React root, so non-JS crawlers (most AI bots, and Google's fallback) see no content. Move apps/site to real static generation: prerender each route's rendered HTML (e.g. vite-react-ssg or a render-to-string step over the existing routes in App.tsx), keeping the SPA hydration path. Emit JSON-LD per page type. This is the foundation every other E15 story builds on.
acceptance_criteria: Every route in App.tsx (/, /install, /directory, /directory/:id, and future E15 routes) is prerendered so its main textual content is present in the served HTML with JS disabled.
Prerendered pages hydrate into the working SPA without content flash or mismatch warnings.
JSON-LD is injected per page type: SoftwareApplication on the homepage, ItemList on /directory, and BreadcrumbList on entry pages; validates against schema.org with no errors.

The per-route title/description/OG/canonical logic from Seo.tsx is reconciled with the build-time prerender so there is one source of truth (no divergence between gen-seo.mjs meta swaps and the runtime Seo component).
The Lighthouse/perf + a11y budget from S13.1 still passes on prerendered pages.
tests: A no-JS fetch of /, /directory, and a /directory/:id page contains the expected headings/body text; JSON-LD blocks parse and validate; hydration produces no console errors.
definition_of_done: Marketing routes serve real, structured content in the initial HTML for crawlers and LLMs.

stories.title: GEO answer layer: llms.txt, extraction-friendly content, FAQ schema
stories.user_story: As an AI assistant summarizing or recommending MCP tooling, I want a machine-readable map of mcpfold plus clean, liftable answer units, so I cite mcpfold accurately when asked about MCP config, discovery, or per-client setup.
stories.context: mcpfold's buyers live inside Claude/ChatGPT/Perplexity, so GEO (generative-engine optimization) is first-class. Ship /llms.txt (concise product + link map) and /llms-full.txt (expanded), structure key pages as short definitional answers and Q&A blocks that LLMs can extract, and add FAQPage JSON-LD. Depends on S15.1 so the content actually exists in HTML; reuses docs content from S13.4 rather than forking it.
acceptance_criteria: /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt are served at the root, following the llms.txt convention: what mcpfold is, the focus terms it answers for, and links to install/docs/directory/guides.
The homepage and each core page carry an extraction-friendly FAQ section (short question + self-contained answer) with FAQPage JSON-LD.
A documented content pattern for answer-first writing (definition in the first sentence, steps as numbered lists, comparisons as tables) is applied to homepage, glossary (S15.6), and guides (S15.5).
robots.txt explicitly allows the major AI crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended) and links the sitemap; the decision is documented.
A lightweight, documented GEO-check procedure exists: a checklist/script of prompts to run against assistants to see whether mcpfold is surfaced (baseline recorded).
tests: llms.txt and llms-full.txt resolve and contain the canonical links; FAQPage JSON-LD validates; robots.txt permits the named AI crawlers and references the sitemap.
definition_of_done: AI answer engines have a clean, structured, permission-granted surface to read and cite.

stories.title: Homepage + core-page on-page SEO and messaging

Add keyword-targeted semantic sections and an internal-linking graph. Copy stays honest and respects no-implied-MCP-endorsement.

The first ~100 words name MCP config, MCP servers, the supported clients (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed), and the token-savings claim.

Below-fold H2 sections each target a cluster (manage every server from one file; works with every MCP client; curate tools/cut context; secrets as references) with the client list rendered as crawlable text/links.
Internal links added from the homepage to /directory, each /guides/<client> page (S15.5), and /glossary (S15.6); an in-repo keyword->page map documents the target term per core page.
The benchmark numbers still come from the committed source (S13.2/S5.4); no copy contradicts docs.
tests: Playwright/asserts: homepage title/H1/meta contain the target terms; client names and internal links to directory/guides/glossary are present; benchmark headline still matches the committed value.
definition_of_done: The homepage is optimized for its focus keyword cluster and anchors the internal-link graph.

stories.title: Directory expansion + category/collection pages (pSEO)
stories.user_story: As someone searching 'best MCP servers' or for a specific server, I want a large, well-organized directory with rich per-server pages and curated collections, so mcpfold is the discovery surface that ranks and gets cited.

Keep the single-source model (packages/core DIRECTORY mirrored to supabase/seed) and neutral, no-endorsement copy. Builds on S15.1 so pages render real content + ItemList schema.
acceptance_criteria: DIRECTORY expands to 150+ curated, deduplicated servers, each with a neutral one-line description, transport + launch, optional tokenRef placeholder, and suggested tags (schema unchanged or extended additively).
Per-server pages carry richer indexable content (what it does, its tools/capabilities where known, and add-to-config snippets) - not just a name + one line.

Programmatic collection pages exist and are prerendered + in the sitemap: a top-level 'Best MCP servers' / directory index and per-category/tag pages (e.g. databases, browser, git, files), each with ItemList JSON-LD and targeted title/H1.
A documented, low-friction process to add or recategorize a server (single source in packages/core, mirrored to seed) with a test guarding the mirror.
Thin/near-duplicate collection pages are avoided: a category page renders only when it has enough distinct entries, else it is omitted or canonicalized; index-bloat guard documented.
tests: DIRECTORY has 150+ valid entries and matches the SQL seed (mirror test); collection + category pages prerender with ItemList schema and appear in the sitemap; an under-populated category is omitted/canonicalized.

stories.title: Per-client 'add MCP servers to <client>' setup guides (pSEO + HowTo)

One page per supported client with HowTo schema; guides link to the directory and homepage.
acceptance_criteria: A /guides/<client> page for each supported client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Zed, and others as adapters land), prerendered with a targeted title/H1 (e.g. 'Add MCP servers to Cursor').
Each guide is generated from the adapter's real facts (config file path per OS, root key, secret strategy, needsRestart) so it stays correct as adapters change - no hand-duplicated config truth.
Each guide has numbered HowTo steps with HowTo JSON-LD, a copy-paste mcpfold command, and links to the directory and install page.

Copy respects no-implied-endorsement and does not misstate any client's format (guarded against the adapter as source of truth).
tests: Each client guide prerenders with correct title/H1 + HowTo schema; the config path/root key/restart facts shown match the adapter's own values (generated, asserted against the registry).
definition_of_done: Every supported client has an authoritative, indexable setup guide targeting its <client> mcp query.

stories.title: Glossary / concept hub for topical authority

Concept pages carry appropriate schema (Article/DefinedTerm) and are prerendered + in the sitemap.
Content is accurate and neutral about the MCP project (no implied affiliation/endorsement).
The hub is internally linked from the homepage and relevant guides/directory pages.

definition_of_done: A definitional concept hub establishes topical authority and a GEO citation surface for the head terms.

stories.title: Comparison / alternatives pages
stories.user_story: As someone evaluating how to manage MCP config across clients, I want honest comparison pages, so I understand where mcpfold fits versus doing it by hand or with other tools - and so assistants have a balanced source to cite.

Pages link into install, directory, and guides, and are in the sitemap.
No unverifiable or disparaging claims about other tools; framing stays neutral and defensible.

stories.title: Technical SEO at scale + search-engine/AI submission + rank & GEO tracking
stories.user_story: As the maintainer, I want the growing set of pages to be technically sound, submitted to search engines, and measured, so programmatic pages get indexed fast and I can see what is ranking and what AI assistants say.

stories.title: Wire CLI_VERSION from package.json at build time
stories.user_story: As a user, I want `mcpfold --version`, telemetry, and the update notifier to report the real published version so the tool doesn't misreport itself and nag about an update on every run.
stories.context: Review finding #1 (blocker). packages/cli/src/version.ts hardcodes `CLI_VERSION = '0.0.0'` with a comment promising S0.4/changesets would wire it from package.json — but nothing does; `build` is just `tsc`. The shipped 1.0.0 binary reports 0.0.0, so update-notifier's isNewer(cache.latest='1.0.0', current='0.0.0') is always true and prints 'Update available' on EVERY command for EVERY user, `mcpfold --version` is wrong, and telemetry cliVersion is useless. Follow-up against S0.4 (done) / S11.1 (done).
